title: Release-candidate check — shopping cart for guests
context: Guests (not signed in) collect products in a cart before checkout; the web shop keeps the cart across page views and the cart API is also used by the mobile app. This story re-checks the same acceptance criteria as TOOL-3 on the release-candidate environment before promotion (story.md#L17, #L19).

sourcesRead.contributes: Acceptance-criteria table (L21-L30, AC-1..AC-8), context and auth (L17, L19), test data (L32). No attachments (L36).

acceptanceCriteria.text: POST /carts creates an empty cart and responds 201 with its id.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: `POST /carts` creates an empty cart and responds 201 with its `id`.
outcomes: POST /carts → 201
the response contains the new cart's id
the new cart is empty (no products)

acceptanceCriteria.text: POST /carts/{id} with product_id and a quantity from 1 to 99 adds the product (200); adding a product already in the cart increases its quantity by the amount added.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: `POST /carts/{id}` with `product_id` and a `quantity` from 1 to 99 adds the product (200); adding a product already in the cart increases its quantity by the amount added.
outcomes: quantity 1 → 200 and the cart contains the product with quantity 1
quantity 99 → 200 and the cart contains the product with quantity 99
adding a product that is already in the cart increases its quantity by the amount added

acceptanceCriteria.text: A quantity outside 1–99 is rejected with 422 and an error for the quantity field; the cart is unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: A quantity outside 1–99 is rejected with 422 and an error for the `quantity` field; the cart is unchanged.
outcomes: quantity 0 → 422
quantity 100 → 422
the response carries an error for the `quantity` field
the cart is unchanged (same products and quantities as before the rejected request)

acceptanceCriteria.text: On a product page, choosing a quantity and pressing "Add to cart" shows "Product added to shopping cart." and the cart icon in the navigation shows the total number of items.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: On a product page, choosing a quantity and pressing "Add to cart" shows "Product added to shopping cart." and the cart icon in the navigation shows the total number of items.
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: a product page of an in-stock product (route: G4)
outcomes: the message "Product added to shopping cart." is shown
the cart icon in the navigation shows the total number of items in the cart (meaning of "total number of items": G5)

acceptanceCriteria.text: The cart page (checkout step 1) lists each product with its quantity, unit price and line total (price × quantity), and the cart total.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: The cart page (checkout step 1) lists each product with its quantity, unit price and line total (price × quantity), and the cart total.
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: the cart page (checkout step 1), reached with products already in the cart (route: G4)
outcomes: every product in the cart is listed with its quantity
every listed product shows its unit price
every listed product shows a line total equal to unit price × quantity
the cart total is shown (how it is computed: G6)

acceptanceCriteria.text: DELETE /carts/{id}/product/{productId} removes the product (204); the cart no longer lists it.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: `DELETE /carts/{id}/product/{productId}` removes the product (204); the cart no longer lists it.
outcomes: DELETE /carts/{id}/product/{productId} → 204
the cart no longer lists the removed product

acceptanceCriteria.text: Deleting a cart responds 204 and is idempotent: deleting a cart that was already deleted also responds 204.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: Deleting a cart responds 204 and is idempotent: deleting a cart that was already deleted also responds 204.
outcomes: deleting a cart → 204
deleting the same, already deleted cart again → 204

acceptanceCriteria.text: Any request for a cart that does not exist responds 404 with the message "Cart not found".
acceptanceCriteria.quote: Any request for a cart that does not exist responds 404 with the message "Cart not found".
outcomes: each request for a cart id that does not exist → 404
the response carries the message "Cart not found"

endpoints.request: product_id and quantity (1 to 99); wrapper/envelope not stated

rules.text: The quantity added to a cart must be from 1 to 99; a quantity outside 1–99 is rejected.
The web shop keeps the cart across page views.

errorModel.case: quantity outside 1–99 when adding a product to a cart
errorModel.body: an error for the quantity field

errorModel.case: any request for a cart that does not exist

auth.mechanism: none: guests are not signed in and carts are anonymous

testData.strategy: Each test creates its own anonymous cart (POST /carts) and deletes it afterwards; products: any product that is in stock (how to find one: G3).
constraints: use only products that are in stock
carts are anonymous: never reuse another test's cart
AC-8 needs a cart id that does not exist (e.g. a cart this test created and deleted), see G7 for DELETE of a cart
testData.cleanup: delete every cart the test created (endpoint: G1)

gaps.element: endpoint (method and path) for deleting a cart

tried.result: L29 says "Deleting a cart" but names no method or path; the only DELETE path given is for removing a product (L28)

gaps.element: endpoint (method and path) for reading a cart's contents (products and quantities)

tried.result: L23 "empty cart", L24 "increases its quantity", L25 "the cart is unchanged", L28 "the cart no longer lists it" and L30 "Any request for a cart" all need the cart's contents or a read request, but no read endpoint is named

gaps.element: how to find an in-stock product (its id for product_id, and its product page)

tried.result: L32: "any product that is in stock"; no product id, lookup endpoint or stock indicator is named

gaps.element: web shop routes and controls: product page, quantity control, cart icon in the navigation, cart page (checkout step 1) and its per-product quantity / unit price / line total and cart total

tried.result: L26 names the "Add to cart" button and the cart icon in the navigation; L27 calls the cart page "checkout step 1"; no routes or other labels

gaps.element: what "the total number of items" on the cart icon counts: the sum of the quantities in the cart, or the number of distinct products

tried.result: L26: "choosing a quantity ... the cart icon in the navigation shows the total number of items"; not defined further

gaps.value: the sum of the quantities of all products in the cart (each unit counts as an item)

gaps.element: how "the cart total" on the cart page is computed (sum of the line totals? anything added or deducted?)

tried.result: L27 defines the line total (price × quantity) but only says "and the cart total", with no formula

gaps.value: the cart total equals the sum of the line totals

gaps.element: conflict: AC-7 (L29) says deleting a cart that was already deleted responds 204; AC-8 (L30) says any request for a cart that does not exist responds 404. Which applies to DELETE of a deleted (or never-created) cart?

tried.result: L29: already-deleted cart → 204; L30: any request for a non-existent cart → 404; neither line says it supersedes the other

gaps.value: AC-7 is the specific exception for deleting a cart: DELETE of an already deleted cart → 204. AC-8 (404, "Cart not found") is checked with the other requests for a non-existent cart (read, add product, remove product). DELETE of a cart id that was never created is not evaluated.

gaps.element: does the 1–99 limit apply to the resulting quantity when a product already in the cart is added again (e.g. a line at 99 plus 1)?

tried.result: L24 bounds the quantity sent in the request and says a repeat add increases the quantity by the amount added; L25 rejects "a quantity outside 1–99"; neither says whether the accumulated quantity is bounded

coverage.note: Target environment (release candidate, AUT profile toolshop-rc) and cross-reference to TOOL-3; the criteria themselves are listed in full at L23-L30 and are cited from there.
Guests not signed in → no auth; "keeps the cart across page views" → R3 (exercised by the AC-4 → AC-5 journey); mobile-app use of the cart API is context.
